title: Both handlers fall back to CloudPostureScan.findById(scanId) with NO organizationId filter when the org-scoped lookup misses, unlike the sibling getScanProgress (line 215) which re-checks scan.organizationId === req.orgId after the identical fallback and throws 403 if not.
description: Route middleware's getScanProjectId (scan.routes.js) is itself org-scoped, so for a foreign-org scanId it returns null; because the route uses requireProjectMembership({...,required:false}), a null result lets the request through instead of blocking it. The unscoped findById fallback then returns the OTHER organization's full scan + findings (or generates a PDF/CSV/Excel export of it). Any authenticated user who learns/guesses another org's scan _id can read or export that org's complete cloud security findings. CONFIRMED by direct code read of all 3 functions + the route middleware chain.
tags: verified-note: Yes - full exploit chain traced and confirmed

title: getScanProgress unconditionally overrides the MongoDB status with the Redis cache's status (status = cacheData.status || dbStatus) with no timestamp/staleness comparison against dbStatus. The Python worker's redis_cache.delete_scan_status() is defined but never called anywhere, so the stale key only expires after a fixed 1-hour TTL.
description: If a Prowler worker crashes mid-scan after writing status:'running' to Redis, scan-reconciler.job.js correctly marks Mongo status:'abandoned' within minutes, but getScanProgress keeps returning the stale cached 'running X%' for up to the remaining hour - the user sees an apparently-live scan that will never move again. CONFIRMED: verified the unconditional override at the exact lines cited.
tags: verified-note: Yes - unconditional cache override confirmed at the exact lines cited

title: None of the frontend's 3 'is this scan done?' terminal-status checks (nor the backend's own progress-percentage switch) include 'abandoned', 'timed_out', or 'completed_with_warnings' - all 3 are real, live terminal statuses (abandoned is set in 5 places by scan-reconciler.job.js; completed_with_warnings/timed_out are real model enum values used elsewhere).
description: Once a scan is marked abandoned/timed_out/completed_with_warnings, the frontend's 15s fallback poll interval never recognizes it as finished and never calls clearInterval - it polls forever for the life of the component, the progress card silently freezes at its last %, and the user never sees a failure/abandoned toast. CONFIRMED: verified all 3 terminal-status arrays are missing all 3 values, and that scan-reconciler.job.js genuinely sets 'abandoned' in 5 code paths.
tags: verified-note: Yes - both cache-override and terminal-status-list gaps directly confirmed
